name: Junko Ōhashi
editorial_article: Junko Ōhashi debuted with her 1974 album Feeling Now and rose to prominence as a vital voice in the Japanese city pop and soul landscape. Her 1978 hit single Tasogare My Love, the theme for the TBS drama Shishi no Gotoku, earned her a Gold Award at the 20th Japan Record Awards. Following a transition from initial hard rock interests, she adopted a soul-infused style inspired by Sérgio Mendes and Janis Joplin. In 1981, she reached number 7 on the Oricon Singles Chart with the track Silhouette Romance, which sold over 500,000 copies and secured a victory at the 24th Japan Record Awards. Throughout her career, she fronted the band Junko Ōhashi & Minoya Central Station, known for balancing intense vocal delivery with tight ensemble arrangements on recordings like the album Rainbow. She remained a fixture in Japanese popular music, appearing in Kōhaku Uta Gassen since 1979 and resuming her career after cancer treatments in 2019 until her death in 2023.
editorial_bio: A legendary Japanese vocalist celebrated for her powerful range and seminal contributions to city pop and soul throughout the late 1970s and 80s.
